## Six years of packages, none of which come apart {visibility="uncounted"}

| Created | Package | What it fixed | What can be reused |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jun 2020 | `EpiNow2` | Real-time $R_t$ | The whole package |
| Oct 2021 | `epinowcast` | Reporting delays | The whole package |
| Jul 2023 | `epidist` | Delay estimation | The whole package |
| Aug 2024 | `primarycensored` | Censoring bias | Stan source, copied in |
| Sep 2024 | `CensoredDistributions.jl` | Censoring bias | The distribution |

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
::: {.callout-important}
Each one found a real problem, fixed it, and left behind another package
that cannot be taken apart. The fix is always a new package.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
- The same structural request has been written down in `EpiNow2` as an
  issue three times in four years. None of them landed
- Sharing a component between two Stan packages means copying its source
  in. Issue **#1268** asks us to do exactly that

::: {.attribution}

## Eleven packages, and four questions {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**What exists**

- 22 repositories, 19 public. 11 hold a Julia package, 10 of those are
  registered in General
- Six distribution packages, all registered. Enough to build on
- `DistributionsInference.jl` is the fit protocol.
  `ComposableTuringIDModels.jl` is the Turing layer
- `ScoringRules.jl` runs and is not registered.
  `GenerationTime.jl` and `ReproductionNumber.jl` are empty repositories

**What holds it together**

- `EpiAwarePackageTools.jl` writes up to 69 files into a package and
  runs nine quality checks, so a package cannot drift from the standard
- Six automatic differentiation configurations run in CI, from one list
  that also generates the badges and the published support table.
  `EpiAwareADTools.jl` holds the workarounds, each one documented
  against the upstream issue that should delete it
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**What we cannot answer**

1. What is the smallest governance an ecosystem can start with?
2. Julia has no rOpenSci. Should it?
3. Who tells a user which backend works for a model built from five
   packages?
4. How do you release twenty packages that have to work together?

::: {.callout-important}
And the one behind all of them. Is there a Julia ecosystem whose users
are mostly not developers? I went looking and could not find one.
:::
